subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should that behavior live in core shared activation or behind a plugin/channel API seam?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, config contract, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to existing room-event paths
options.body: Document or improve ambient always-on room events and message-tool-only replies instead of adding a new LLM decision state machine.

options.title: Move behind plugin/API design
options.body: Defer core activation until a trusted observation or decision hook can safely support this as a plugin-owned capability.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history across group activation, mention-policy, and current group-gating paths.
